content: Charity Hospital is one of two teaching hospitals that are part of the Medical Center of Louisiana at New Orleans (MCLNO). It is one of several public hospitals in Louisiana managed by the Louisiana State University System. Both Charity Hospital and the nearby University Hospital are teaching hospitals affiliated with the LSU Health Sciences Center in New Orleans (LSUHSC-NO). Charity Hospital is situated in the New Orleans Hospital District, located on the opposite side of Interstate 10 from the LSU Health Sciences Center. Its address is 1532 Tulane Avenue, New Orleans, Louisiana, 70112-1352, and the contact number is (504) 903-2311. Charity Hospital was established on May 10, 1736, through a grant from Jean Louis, a French sailor and shipbuilder who passed away in New Orleans the year prior. In his will, he allocated funds to create a hospital for the indigent population of New Orleans. For over 250 years, this hospital has served the poor in the city. Initially, it was named the Hospital of Saint John or L’Hôpital des Pauvres de la Charité (French for Hospital for the Poor). The first location of Charity Hospital was at the intersection of Chartres Street and Bienville Street in what is now the French Quarter. The hospital was founded 18 years after New Orleans was established by France in 1718. It is the second-oldest continuously operating public hospital in the United States, with only Bellevue Hospital in New York City being older, having been founded on March 31, 1736. The original facility of Charity Hospital quickly became insufficient, leading to the construction of a second hospital on Basin Street in 1743. A third hospital was built nearby in 1785 and was renamed San Carlos Hospital in honor of King Charles III of Spain after New Orleans was ceded to Spain in 1763. However, this hospital was destroyed by fire in 1809. In the aftermath, temporary facilities were set up at the Cabildo for one month, then at the Jourdan residence in the Faubourg Marigny for six months, and finally at the dilapidated De La Vergne plantation for five years. A fourth hospital was constructed on Canal Street, where the Fairmont Hotel now stands, and was completed in 1815. However, this facility was widely criticized for being inadequate and underfunded. In 1832, a fifth hospital was built within the boundaries of Girod, Gravier, St. Mary, and Common Streets in the Faubourg St. Marie. This hospital came under the administration of the Sisters of Charity, who managed it for the next century. Under their leadership, Charity Hospital became a renowned institution for medical care in New Orleans. By the 20th century, the city’s rapid expansion and increasing demand for medical services for the indigent population necessitated the construction of a sixth hospital. This new facility, located on Tulane Avenue, was completed in 1939. With 2,680 beds, it was the second-largest hospital in the United States at the time. Adjacent to this hospital, the LSU Health Sciences Center in New Orleans (LSUHSC-NO) was built in 1931. In 1970, the Louisiana Department of Health and Human Resources (DHH) assumed control of Charity Hospital. In 1991, the hospital was transferred to the Louisiana Health Care Authority (LHCA), and in 1997, it came under the management of the LSU System. During Hurricane Katrina, Charity Hospital sustained significant flood damage, similar to its sister institution, University Hospital. The evacuation of patients from the flooded hospital garnered national attention. Following the storm, a temporary clinic named the Spirit of Charity was established at the Convention Center. This clinic was later relocated to the New Orleans Centre building near the Superdome. By February 2007, a renovated University Hospital had taken over the emergency care responsibilities that Charity Hospital had previously provided. The future of Charity Hospital remains uncertain. LSUHSC has announced plans to construct a new, modern facility nearby, named the Medical Center of Louisiana at New Orleans (MCLNO). If funding is approved by the Louisiana State Legislature, this new hospital would consolidate the functions of both Charity Hospital and University Hospital.
